Friday 23 October 2026 · 24 stories
Morning Brief
Nifty 50 fell 0.54% to 22,688 and decliners led 1,845 to 696
Today’s read
The biggest names carried the session. The fifty most traded stocks returned -0.18% weighted by turnover, against -1.24% for the median stock, a gap of 1.1 percentage points, so most stocks did worse than the busiest names suggest.

Sunteck Realty Limited rose 5.3% on 162 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about fund raising, “Issuance of Commercial Paper of Rs. 70 crores”.

Tata Teleservices (Maharashtra) Limited rose 18.6% on 160 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “Stocks in news: Swiggy, Infosys, HPCL, eMudhra, Adani Power, Shriram Finance, Tata Motors and NLC India”.

The exchange has formally asked 1 company to explain today's move: DCM Shriram Industries Limited. Those queries were filed after the close, so they confirm the move rather than explain it. NSE's own surveillance flagged the same names.

Nothing in the news or in exchange filings explains the volume in The India Cements Limited (434x), Optimus Finance Limited (192x), DCM Shriram Industries Limited (157x). That usually points to a sector story rather than a company one.

What happened
Breaking
India's interest rate gap with G7 in focus as RBI weighs inflation risks: Report
A narrowing policy rate differential between the Reserve Bank of India and developed central banks limits domestic monetary easing room. This spread compresses currency returns and dampens foreign debt flows, weakening the rupee. Elevated borrowing costs will therefore persist for non-banking financial companies and real estate developers, constraining net interest margins and delaying corporate balance sheet deleveraging.
ET Economy · +2 others
MPC minutes: Two more interest rate hikes on cards, maybe even a third
The latest monetary policy minutes point to two additional 25-basis-point rate increases by February, with a third likely if crude stays elevated. Higher policy rates will accelerate deposit repricing across commercial banks, compressing net interest margins in subsequent quarters. The resulting rise in retail borrowing rates will pressure credit growth across housing and auto finance lenders.
ET Markets · +2 others
Rupee declines first time in eight sessions as Brent oil prices rise above $112
The rupee broke a seven-day advance as Brent crude climbed above $112 per barrel, overshadowing primary equity market inflows. Expensive crude expands India's current account deficit and inflates feedstock costs for downstream paint manufacturers, tyre makers and state-run oil marketing companies. Weekly trade deficit prints and refinery crude intake figures will confirm whether import costs remain at these elevated levels.

India’s copper demand up 12% in FY26 at 2,100 KT led by automotive, infra & realty sectors
Domestic copper demand will reach 2,100 kilotonnes in FY26, expanding 12% on higher automotive and infrastructure activity. This secular consumption growth expands volume off-take for wire and cable makers such as Polycab and KEI Industries, alongside primary producers like Hindalco. However, operating margins for domestic fabricators will remain exposed to international spot copper prices and treatment charges given persistent domestic smelting deficits.

Neocloud short sellers rack up $6 billion as AI debt fears deepen
Short sellers gained $6 billion betting against debt-laden US artificial intelligence cloud providers as capital expenditure and leverage scrutiny escalated. The sell-off signals caution for Indian tier-one IT service providers, as enterprise clients defer speculative software experimentation to conserve cash. It also threatens to raise international borrowing costs and tighten debt covenants for domestic data centre builders financing graphics processing unit clusters.

Navitas Solar raised $20 million to set up a 2.2-gigawatt solar cell manufacturing unit. Domestic cell capacity reduces supply-chain dependence on Chinese imports for listed module manufacturers like Waaree Energies and Premier Energies. Commissioning timelines and raw silicon procurement costs will determine whether this new capacity pressures domestic cell margins next year.

Apple stock rises 28% in 2026 as AI stocks wobble: Why investors are betting on the iPhone maker
Apple shares rose 28% in 2026 as global capital rotated away from capital-intensive AI infrastructure into cash-generative tech. High consumer demand and iPhone production shifts to India directly benefit domestic electronic manufacturing services companies like Dixon Technologies and Foxconn vendors through higher order volumes. Monthly Indian electronics export data will confirm if assembly revenues sustain this momentum.

Traders ditch derivatives for broker-funded stock bets
Retail leverage is shifting from index derivatives to broker margin trading facilities following higher taxes and larger contract sizes. The migration supports net interest income and spread revenues for retail-focused brokerages such as Angel One and Motilal Oswal. It also concentrates leverage into cash equities, increasing price volatility across heavily margined mid-cap and small-cap stocks.

Banking liquidity surplus shrinks to Rs 541 crore as cash crunch increases
Banking system liquidity contracted to 541 crore rupees, pushing the weighted average call money rate to 5.65%, 15 basis points above the repo rate. Tighter interbank cash raises marginal funding costs for banks and non-bank lenders reliant on wholesale certificates of deposit. Reserve Bank variable rate repo auction announcements over the coming days will confirm whether this pressure persists.
ET Markets
Government plans to pare stakes in 4 PSU banks to 75%
The government plans to trim equity holdings across four state-owned lenders to meet the 25% minimum public shareholding rule. Looming offers for sale create secondary supply overhangs that cap valuation multiples for lenders like Central Bank of India, Indian Overseas Bank and UCO Bank. The floor discount announced in the first prospective offer will reveal institutional pricing appetite.
ET Markets
Gold falls to more than two-month low as oil-fuelled inflation fears weigh
Gold fell to a two-month low as oil-driven inflation concerns supported US Treasury yields and the dollar. Higher American yields tighten global financial conditions, dampening foreign institutional flows into Indian equities and softening the rupee. Weaker bullion prices also narrow collateral buffers and loan growth momentum for gold-financing companies such as Muthoot Finance and Manappuram Finance.

Kent RO invests ₹250 cr in Noida plant for solar inverters, lithium batteries, targets ₹1,750 cr revenue in FY27
Kent New Energy commissioned a ₹250 crore facility in Noida to produce 3.5 GWh of solar hybrid inverters and lithium battery packs, targeting ₹1,750 crore revenue by FY27. This move intensifies domestic supply competition for listed battery and inverter makers like Exide Industries and Amara Raja Energy. Success will depend on FY26 revenue execution and client wins in the residential rooftop solar segment.

Himadri Speciality Chemicals plans ₹1,613 crore capacity expansion across key businesses
Himadri Speciality Chemical announced a ₹1,613 crore capex plan, directing ₹1,125 crore toward lithium iron phosphate cathode materials and the rest into speciality carbon black and chemicals. The pivot into high-margin EV battery components alters the company's valuation profile away from traditional coal tar pitch. Key monitoring points include commercialization timelines and off-take agreements with domestic cell manufacturers over the next two years.

UBS acquires 4.8% stake in wealth manager 360 ONE WAM through warrant exercise
UBS exercised 2.05 crore warrants to acquire a 4.8% equity stake in 360 ONE WAM for ₹1,584 crore. The transaction completes the absorption of UBS's onshore Indian wealth management desk into 360 ONE WAM, boosting assets under management and recurring fee income. Equity dilution is offset by capital inflows, supporting organic expansion in domestic wealth management.

Adani Total Gas Q2 Results: Net profit rises 6% YoY to Rs 173 crore, revenue jumps 34%
Adani Total Gas reported a 5.9% year-on-year net profit increase to ₹173.27 crore for Q2, despite revenue rising 33.8% to ₹2,109.65 crore. Profitability lagged top-line growth because lower domestic APM gas allocations forced reliance on costlier imported LNG, compressing gross margins per standard cubic meter. Volume growth across city gas distribution networks remains critical to offsetting input cost inflation.

Indian refiners increased Middle Eastern crude imports to a 19-month high in September as discounts on Russian Urals crude narrowed. Reduced Russian savings squeeze gross refining margins for downstream state-run refiners IOCL, BPCL, and HPCL, alongside Reliance Industries, by raising overall raw material procurement costs.
